title: Electromagnetics & Basic Electricity
summary: Units and constants, Faraday/Lenz/Fleming, magnetic circuits, inductance, resistance and temperature, capacitors, magnetic materials.
definitions: Induced EMF opposes the change that produces it (energy conservation).
Generator: thumb motion, first finger field, second finger induced current.
Motor: direction of force on a current-carrying conductor.
Opposition to flux, S = l/(μA) (AT/Wb) — like resistance.
Energy lost per cycle per unit volume.
Above it a ferromagnet becomes paramagnetic (iron ≈ 770 °C).
formulas: R = ρl/A;  R_t = R0(1 + α t)
Φ = MMF/S,  MMF = NI,  S = l/(μ0μr A)
facts: μ0 = 4π × 10⁻⁷ H/m; ε0 = 8.854 × 10⁻¹² F/m; electron charge 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
Units: flux Wb, flux density T (Wb/m²), H in A/m, MMF in AT, reluctance AT/Wb, inductance H.
Analogy: MMF ↔ EMF, flux ↔ current, reluctance ↔ resistance, permeance ↔ conductance.
Metals: positive temperature coefficient; semiconductors: negative; manganin/constantan ≈ zero.
Diamagnetic μr < 1 (bismuth, copper); paramagnetic slightly > 1 (aluminium); ferromagnetic ≫ 1 (Fe, Ni, Co).
Permanent magnets: high retentivity and coercivity (wide loop). Transformer cores: narrow loop (soft).
In series, a 60 W lamp glows brighter than a 100 W lamp (higher resistance).
traps: Doubling the length of a wire by stretching gives 4R, not 2R.

examples.q: Coils 4 H and 9 H, k = 0.5. Find M and series-aiding/opposing inductance.
